title: Agentic task prompt v4 — GOAL/TESTS/LOOP with durable operations and per-test verification binding
description: Additive successor to prompt.schema.v3.json, which is retained byte-unchanged so already-accepted v3 prompt records keep validating unmodified: every field v4 adds is optional, and a v3 document with no per-test verifier is a valid v4 document that simply means 'every test is checked inline by the prompt-level agent.' Version 4 closes a gap v3 left open: v3's operations contract states how the run is journaled and gated, but nothing bound an individual TEST to a specific checker. Without that binding, a TEST whose check text says 'have Codex review this' is schema-indistinguishable from one that actually invokes .claude/skills/qa-gate-codex-run's bounded, session-audited protocol versus one that free-hands 'codex exec' inline — the exact self-grading gap qa-gate-codex-run's own SKILL.md states Claude cannot close by itself. v4 adds an optional per-test verifier, reusing one $defs/executor block for both the prompt-level agent and any test's verifier (single or fanned-out) so there is one closed vocabulary for 'who/what runs this,' not two. This only makes the obligation textually undeniable in the document (schema-checkable, auditable) — it cannot force the runtime agent to actually invoke what it declares; that guarantee still comes from the named skill/subagent itself.
$comment: INSTANCE FORMAT: any agent asked to write a file compliant with this schema MUST author it as YAML, not JSON — filename <slug>.prompt.v<N>.yaml, first line `# yaml-language-server: $schema=<relative path to this file>`. This is an authoring instruction for the agent, not something the JSON Schema validator itself checks: $comment is never evaluated during validation, and a validator handed already-parsed data cannot see the source filename, the first line, or which serialization produced it. Mechanical enforcement of this policy is a separate, explicit step: schemas/validate_instance.py --schema <this file> --instance <path> checks the filename pattern, the yaml-language-server directive (resolved to a canonical path and compared against --schema), that the file parses as YAML, and only then validates the parsed data against this schema.

model.description: Model family used by the prompt-level agent. inherit is an explicit unpinned choice, not silence.

agent.description: The prompt-level default executor. Still required (v2's own rationale holds: a prompt with no stated executor at all is underspecified) but execution_path may now be the explicit value 'inherit' — an auditable statement of 'not pinned' rather than the field being silently absent. subagent_type and agent_ref are mutually exclusive: a claude_code_subagent must be traceable to exactly one of a known built-in type or a specific external agent definition file, never ambiguous between the two.

executor.description: Who/what runs a check: the 'who' (execution_path/subagent_type/agent_ref/model) and the 'what' (invokes) as two independent axes on one reusable block, used for the prompt-level agent, a single test verifier, and each branch of a fan_out verifier alike.

model.description: Optional. Overrides the prompt-level model for this executor only (meaningful on a test verifier or fan_out branch; on the prompt-level agent this is redundant with the sibling top-level model field and should be omitted).

subagent_type.description: A known built-in subagent type name (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'Explore', 'fork'). Mutually exclusive with agent_ref.

agent_ref.description: Path to an external custom agent definition (.claude/agents/<name>.md) instead of a built-in subagent_type. Mutually exclusive with subagent_type.

invokes.description: Optional. What this executor actually runs, beyond inline reasoning. Absent means the executor performs the check itself inline (equivalent to invokes.type=inline_check).

invocation.description: What the executor runs: an inline check it performs itself, a named skill (e.g. qa-gate-codex-run), or another prompt (recursive composition — the same pattern implementation.graph.v<N>.yaml already uses when a plan-graph node names its own prompt file).

skill.description: Required when type is skill. The exact skill name (e.g. 'qa-gate-codex-run'), not a paraphrase — a check whose text merely describes similar behavior without naming this field is not schema-bound to actually invoking it.

prompt_path.description: Required when type is prompt. Path to another GOAL/TEST/LOOP prompt file, canonical YAML only (*.prompt.v<N>.yaml or .yml) — markdown and JSON prompt instances are no longer accepted for new nested-prompt references, per this schema's own $comment. That file must itself validate against a prompt schema; this test's pass/fail is that nested prompt's own loop reaching its own stopping_condition.

verifier.description: Optional, per-test. Absent means this test is checked inline by the prompt-level agent (today's v3 behavior, unchanged). Present means either one executor overriding the default for this test alone, or a fan_out of several executors whose individual results are combined by aggregation.

aggregation.description: How the fanned-out executors' individual results combine into this test's single pass/fail. any_of and majority let a lenient reviewer overrule a correct rejection, which defeats an adversarial gate's purpose — a fan_out whose branches include invokes.type=skill with skill=qa-gate-codex-run should use all_of.

operations_executor.description: Unchanged from prompt.schema.v3.json's $defs/executor, renamed operations_executor here only to free the name 'executor' for the broader who/what block v4 introduces above. This still describes the journal/gate implementation, not who verifies a test.
